app.title: HDV Disposition Optimizer (Heavy-Duty-Vehicle Fleet Disposition Optimizer)
app.summary: A person checks the four input workbooks (fleet, depot, energy prices, orders) and the files derived from them, such as routed trips, price curves and a solar generation curve, and rebuilds the derived files when needed. They set the cost, efficiency, battery, crew-rule and solver parameters, then choose a run type. Disposition plans one dated day for the existing fleet. Asset Sizing picks one fleet and the chargers it needs for a range of days. Scenario Sweep solves every combination of chosen scenario axes for every day. The solver runs in the background, showing its progress and a stop button. The results show cost, energy, grid-peak and crew metrics, a per-step schedule and schedule figures for one solve, along with charts comparing the solves. Each table can be downloaded as CSV, and past run summaries can be opened again from disk.

task.text: Work out the lowest-cost way to dispatch a mixed diesel and battery truck fleet over a day's orders, including charging and V2G, or size the fleet and chargers a range of days would need, and compare scenarios.

data.text: Spreadsheet workbooks: a vehicle roster with battery and consumption figures, depot charging stations, metered site load and a PV plant, yearly and hourly energy prices, and an order book with pickup, delivery and time windows. These become routed trips and price curves on a 30-minute grid, and each solve produces a schedule and a summary row.
data.item: a transport order routed into a trip on one operating day, assigned to a vehicle on a 30-minute grid

stage.text: planning a fleet's day and sizing its assets with an optimization model, then comparing scenarios

mechanism.text: Five numbered tabs lead from inputs through settings to a run, then results. The run tab changes its controls with the run type, starts a background mixed-integer solve, and polls it for progress. The results tab redraws the same metric rows for the current session's run and for any summary CSV read back from disk, and a picker opens any one solve of a range or sweep in detail.

field.text: mixed-integer optimization of electric truck fleet dispatch and charging in transport and energy systems engineering

workflow.name: set up and solve an optimization model, then compare its runs

steps.here: Four Excel workbooks are shown sheet by sheet. Rebuild derived inputs regenerates the routed trips, price curves, depot load and PVGIS cache, with an optional forced re-route. A date picker draws a preview of the PV curve against the depot load.

Number inputs set the MIP gap, time cap, working hours, demand charge, grid fees, tolls, charging efficiencies, battery degradation, crew rules and penalties. A configuration panel shows the effective parameter set and can download it.

A segmented control picks the run type. Disposition takes one date that has trips. Asset Sizing and Scenario Sweep take a day-range slider. The sweep also has multiselects for years, cost scenarios, V2G and external charging, with a count of the solves this will make. Sizing adds a slider for the fleet-search time budget.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Run Optimization starts a background solver process. A spinner shows how far the run has got, for example '3 of 12', and a stop button ends it. The finished payload is stored in session state.

Metric rows give solver status and gap, operating cost, energy, V2G, degradation, tolls, grid peak, PV use, conversion losses, empty running, drivers and chargers. Below them come the per-step schedule and schedule figures. A selectbox opens any solve of a range.

A sweep's solves are listed in one table. A measure picker plots cost against the axes that changed, with year on the x axis and the other axes as series. A sizing run shows the fleet it chose, the chargers needed by rank, and the busiest day.

Buttons download the schedule, range or sweep summary, charging infrastructure and configuration as CSV. Every run writes a stamped summary CSV, and Previous Results reopens it at full depth together with that run's own figures.

distinctive: The disposition date sets the trips, the depot's seasonal baseline load and the PV yield all at once, so they cannot disagree with each other.
Asset Sizing picks one shared fleet for a whole range of days, trading ownership cost against operating cost. Chargers are not optimized; they are read off the finished schedules by rank.
A sweep runs every combination of year, cost scenario, V2G and external charging for every day, and states the number of solves before the run starts.
Results distinguish proved, gap-optimal and time-limited solves. Steering penalties and driver salary are reported apart from the objective.
Disposition runs use the daily price sheet as written, and sizing and sweep runs rescale it onto a scenario year and band, so the Disposition tab hides the controls that would change nothing.
